chunk-001:chunk001-c01.proposition: Neither causal determination nor indeterminacy permits a person to be the ultimate author or controller of an action.

orphanFallback.rationale: The passage independently advances the foundational dilemma that prior causation locates ultimate origins outside the person while randomness supplies no control.

chunk-001:chunk001-c07.proposition: The felt immediacy of an experience cannot establish its interpretation, because introspection can present illusory forces or agencies as real.

orphanFallback.rationale: The centrifugal-force example independently establishes that compelling introspective appearances can be misinterpreted, limiting their ability to prove genuine volitional control.

chunk-001:chunk001-c08.proposition: Attention to deliberation reveals thoughts, options, and rational conclusions presenting themselves rather than being proactively selected by a chooser.

orphanFallback.rationale: The city exercise independently supports an unchosen-content account of deliberation in which alternatives arise and conclusions compel without proactive selection.

chunk-001:chunk001-c09.proposition: Agent causation does not end the explanatory regress, because conscious actions follow unchosen desires and the strongest operative desire governs behavior.

orphanFallback.rationale: The drinking and gym examples independently explain apparently reluctant action through competing desires whose relative strength the person did not choose.

chunk-002:chunk002-c06.proposition: Agent causation does not explain control because a mental event either has determining causes beyond the agent's ultimate control or occurs causelessly and randomly.

orphanFallback.rationale: The passage independently applies the caused-or-random dilemma to mental events and therefore supplies a complete objection to unexplained agent causation.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-04.proposition: Libertarian free will requires a genuine ability to act differently in physically identical circumstances, for which no differentiating explanation is available.

orphanFallback.rationale: The two-identical-universes example independently defines the disputed alternate-possibilities requirement and poses the explanatory challenge for divergent choices.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-09.proposition: Introspective confidence in free will is defeasible when philosophical considerations provide alternative explanations of the apparent experience.

orphanFallback.rationale: The passage independently distinguishes reasonable everyday perceptual trust from treating introspection alone as decisive proof after an alternative explanation is supplied.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-10.proposition: The alternate-possibilities conception of free will is philosophically incoherent regardless of whether consciousness is material, immaterial, or emergent.

orphanFallback.rationale: The passage independently makes the conceptual objection theory-neutral, expressly declining to depend on materialism, neuroscience, or a particular account of consciousness.

chunk-004:chunk004-c08.proposition: Even conscious conduct under coercion remains technically a choice between desire-governed alternatives, although ordinary language reasonably describes it as forced.

orphanFallback.rationale: The wallet example independently shows how conscious alternative-sensitive conduct can remain structured by prevailing desires under coercive and social pressure.
